references.text: In [ref:Joh 4:50|John 4:50], the royal official believes Jesus' word that his son will live and sets out for home. Verse 52 shows that on the way he inquires about the exact time of the healing to confirm the power of Jesus' words.
In [ref:Joh 4:53|John 4:53], it is confirmed that the time given by the father—the seventh hour—was exactly when Jesus had said, "your son lives". This led to faith for his entire household.

In [ref:Mark 1:30-31|Mark 1:30-31], Jesus heals Simon Peter's mother-in-law from fever (πυρετός), the same Greek word used in John 4:52. The fever left her, just as it had left the royal official's son.
In [ref:Luk 4:38-39|Luke 4:38-39], Jesus heals a woman with a high fever, and the fever leaves her. The expression "the fever left" (ἀφῆκεν ... ὁ πυρετός) is parallel to John 4:52.

In [ref:Matt 8:13|Matthew 8:13], Jesus heals the officer's servant from a distance, and the servant was made well "at that very hour". This is a close parallel to the healing in John 4, where the son was healed exactly at the time Jesus spoke.

[ref:Joh 2:11|John 2:11] describes Jesus' first sign in Cana of Galilee. The healing of the official's son is mentioned in [ref:Joh 4:54|John 4:54] as the second sign, and the confirmation of the time in verse 52 underscores the miraculous nature of the sign.
